title: Turn 34, and the window isn't full
spec: U08 · compaction, and the audit of what survived it
intro: A review session degrades at 31% window utilisation, gets compacted, and then gets audited: which decisions and open issues survived the collapse, and which one quietly dissolved.
foot: Do it for real: ask Q1, Q3, Q6 and Q9 in one naive session and watch the sparkline climb; refresh and repeat in notes.

steps.title: The session is failing at 31% full
narrative: A reviewer has been working the MedFlow queue for thirty-four turns. Nothing has errored, the window is nowhere near its limit — and at turn 31 the copilot re-asked a question that was answered at turn 6.

This is context rot in its session form. The failure axis is signal-to-noise, not size: the answer is still in the window, buried under twenty-eight turns of tool dumps, resolved detours and pleasantries. A bigger window buries it deeper.
steps.youDo: Open the session strip and read the sparkline rather than the last answer. The shape of the curve is the diagnosis.

before.title: ILLUSTRATIVE — a long session, nowhere near the limit

view.label: 200K window · turn 34
view.note: 31% full and already re-asking answered questions. Capacity was never the constraint — this is an illustrative session shape, not a bench cell.

steps.title: Why the curve climbs and never comes down
narrative: The single-call receipts do show the engine of the climb. In naive mode every call re-sends the whole domain dump: Q1's retrieved layer is 1,612 tokens, and so is Q3's, Q6's, and Q9's. That block is re-paid on every turn, and the history layer is added on top of it.

So the naive session cost is not the median of its receipts — it is the sum, plus a history term that grows quadratically with turn count. The four bench questions alone re-carry the same 1,612-token dump four times over.
steps.claudeSays: Nothing decides to forget. An append-only session has no eviction policy, so every turn's material is still competing for attention on turn 34.

before.title: MEASURED — naive's retrieved layer, four questions

cells: Q6 · why PA-1004 went to review

steps.title: Compact: rewrite the case board
narrative: Compaction distils the transcript-so-far into a summary and replaces the raw history with it. What must survive is precise: decisions made, open issues, and load-bearing identifiers. What is meant to dissolve: resolved detours, duplicate tool dumps, and conversation about the conversation.
Run it as its own clean call. Asking the main model to summarise the very context it is drowning in is the classic own-goal — the compactor inherits the rot it was hired to remove.
steps.youDo: Trigger compaction on a cadence, not at the cliff — the compactor needs a healthy context to do its job.

terminal.text: compact(turns=34, keep_recent=2) → clean call, not in-session
extracted  3 decisions, 2 open items, 7 load-bearing ids
discarded 21 routine turns (chatter, resolved detours, tool dumps)
✓ history 58,900 → 640 tokens · 2 recent turns kept verbatim

after.title: AFTER — the case board plus two recent turns

view.label: 200K window · after compaction
view.note: The flattening is the point. What you must now prove is that the collapse kept the load-bearing content.

steps.title: The audit: what survived, what dissolved
narrative: Compaction is a lossy operation you performed on your own memory, so it needs the same scrutiny as U07's compressors. Do not read the summary and nod at it — audit it against a list of things that were required to survive.

The audit has three tiers. Decisions and open issues must survive verbatim. Load-bearing identifiers — request ids, member ids, scores — must appear literally, because a paraphrase of PA-1004 is not PA-1004. Everything else is allowed to go, and most of it should.

cells: PA-1002: wait for the EMG before re-scoring
PA-1010: borderline at 50 — keep in review
M-2002 is STANDARD tier, surgical not covered
Eligibility confusion — resolved, tier covers it
4KB of raw queue JSON, re-read three times

steps.title: The open issue that dissolved
narrative: The summariser kept both decisions and rewrote the open items as "a few requests remain pending review" — accurate, fluent, and useless. PA-1004 has a deadline attached to it; "a few requests" does not.

This is exactly the shape of U07's voided saving, moved from the retrieved layer to the history layer. A compaction that loses an open issue has not compressed the session; it has closed it. So compaction gets the same treatment compression got: an assertion that runs before the board is allowed to replace the transcript.
steps.youDo: Break it on purpose in the U08 lab: compact away an open item and watch the assertion refuse the board.

terminal.text: ⏸  ASSERT — every decision and open item present verbatim

✕ compaction lost: 'PA-1004: conservative-management window ends 2026-09-23'
         board REFUSED — history left intact, compaction retried with open items pinned

before.title: BEFORE — ships whatever the summariser produced

after.title: AFTER — decisions and open items must survive verbatim

lines: assert t['text'] in board, f"compaction lost: {t['text']!r}"

steps.title: What the single-call receipts can and cannot tell you
narrative: Be honest about the evidence. The shipped grid is single-call: one question, one assembly, one receipt. It cannot measure multi-turn pressure at all, which is why this walkthrough's session numbers are labelled illustrative rather than dressed up as bench cells.

What the grid can show is the destination compaction is heading toward. The notes arm keeps its established facts outside the window and loads them back as a small history layer: Q1 answers at 141 tokens, of which only 64 is history, and the arm holds a 197.5-token median at 10/10 correct against naive's 1,696 at 9/10. Compaction bends the curve; notes moves the memory off the curve entirely.

The rule to carry into U09: compaction preserves the thread, notes preserve the facts. Pick by task shape — a clinician arguing one borderline determination wants the thread; a reviewer clearing a queue wants the facts.
